neighbours.label: the predicate right after an ambient/dummy 'it' (it rained, it is snowing, it gets dark, it got cold, it took six weeks, what it takes); weather or nightfall phrased without the empty 'it', and referential 'it', stay quiet
neighbours.short: predicate of ambient 'it' (it rained / gets dark / takes)
fire: By noon it rained so hard the streets flooded.
It snowed for three days before the pass reopened.
In December it gets dark before five o'clock.
After the sun went down it got cold very quickly.
She has what it takes to lead the team.
It took the crew six weeks to repair the bridge.
It was raining when the train finally arrived.
Up in the mountains it is snowing again.
quiet: By noon the rain was so heavy the streets flooded.
Snow fell for three days before the pass reopened.
In December darkness comes before five o'clock.
After the sun went down the air got cold very quickly.
She has the skills needed to lead the team.
The crew needed six weeks to repair the bridge.
The rain was falling when the train finally arrived.
Up in the mountains the snow keeps falling again.
neighbours.notes: Step-out feeder of bonsai1/L5/N6367- (late), drop 0.12 by single-unit zero ablation. Exploration probes: referential 'it' (it bored me, it ran away, it worked) ~0; 'he takes' 0; weather without 'it' (the storm raged, the weather turned cold, the sky rained ash) ~0; ambient 'it is late/quiet' fires mildly (0.15-0.22), ambient verbs strongest. 'it seems' and 'it stopped' were quiet, so not every expletive-it predicate. These exact sentences were probed during exploration before pre-registration. The inverse-solver round crashed (toolchain JSON serialization error), so no leak search was run.
